Question B-003-018-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Turning off and unplugging removes the mains source before any inspection or fault check begins.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "turn off the power and unplug the power cord": This is the correct choice because turning off and unplugging removes the mains source before any inspection or fault check begins.
- sourceIndex 1: "short out the leads of the filter capacitor": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from turn off the power and unplug the power cord. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, that component has a specific circuit role, but it is not the energy source or safety item being asked for.
- sourceIndex 2: "check the action of the capacitor bleeder resistance": This answer would fit a different fault than turn off the power and unplug the power cord. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, that component has a specific circuit role, but it is not the energy source or safety item being asked for.
- sourceIndex 3: "remove and check the fuse from the power supply": This option confuses another station topic with turn off the power and unplug the power cord. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
